name: MedQA
description: A medical question answering benchmark based on the United States Medical Licensing Examination (USMLE) questions, testing clinical knowledge across basic science, clinical science, and patient care. Questions are multiple-choice (4–5 options) drawn from USMLE Steps 1, 2, and 3. Also includes MCMLE (Chinese medical licensing exam) and TWMLE (Taiwan) variants.
typical_sota_score: ~90–95% (frontier models as of 2025–2026; passing score for physicians ~60%)
reputation: Most widely used medical LLM benchmark; published by MIT/Harvard; clinical milestone: LLMs passing USMLE marked a turning point in medical AI; 2025 research found it most predictive of clinical performance (Spearman rho=0.59)
notes: Passing score for physician licensure is approximately 60%. Med-PaLM 2 (Google Health) was first to exceed physician passing score. Frontier models now score 90%+. 2025 research found MedQA most predictive of clinical performance (Spearman rho=0.59) among medical benchmarks. However, 7.4% of questions found unfit due to errors or ambiguity. MedMCQA (187K questions from Indian medical exams) is a large-scale alternative.
